concreteNamedSourceContexts.text: The rail is the default. Each pinned Space is an independently selectable, named item, followed by access to the Spaces browser. The browser exposes all authorised Spaces and the existing create/edit/manage actions, including unpinned built-ins and nested user-created Spaces. Pinning, unpinning and reordering preserve SpaceID; names are not identities.

A Spaces tab MUST have stable TabID, target type/identity, source Space/context, current view mode and restorable navigation state. Targets include canonical conversations, images/artifacts, registered AppSurfaces and safe Generative UI surfaces. Ordinary Open focuses an existing equivalent target tab; an explicit new-view action may open another view of the same canonical entity. Tabs support select, close, reorder and keyboard navigation.

The visual editor MUST expose + Add for a section, chat/reference, app/CUI/Generative UI surface, or authorised Plugin/Automation action. Users can rename, configure, move, reorder and remove custom entries and sections. Dragging rearranges items and sections, including moving an item between sections. Keyboard/touch alternatives, undo and Reset to Default are required. The example's remove controls remove sidebar organisation only, not the underlying chats or assignments.

The floating usage bar is anchored to the bottom of the chat-list area without covering list items or the composer. It shows the actual configured 9to1 windows and any limits a connected provider can measure; daily, weekly and monthly are supported window types, not permission to invent a limit the account does not have. Compact summaries expand into source-labelled details.

The listed Study sidebar is its default layout under the shared custom-sidebar system, not a private second sidebar implementation. Planner opens the canonical Study burrow in an embedded Planner tab. My Progress opens the existing topic tracker, and Revision Bank opens the resource catalogue below.

Recommended, All, Flashcards, Notes, Papers and Quizzes are the default category tabs. Custom categories such as Homework have stable IDs and configurable order. Automatic creation of a category for an uncovered material type is opt-in and idempotent. Categories are filters/membership views, not duplicated artifacts. Recommended draws from recorded difficult/neglected topics and authorised linked resources, with an honest empty state when no match exists.

Resources open in the real owning-app viewer/interactor embedded in Spaces, with an explicit switch to permitted editing. Open in App is available from both resource and tab context menus and an accessible non-right-click route. Both views address the same artifact. Missing apps/modules follow LE-02; revoked sources cannot remain readable through cached previews or recommendations.

Study has one canonical Study burrow per owning Study scope, created idempotently and referenced by ID rather than the display name. A custom Minecraft burrow is an independent user-created context. Study's Planner button opens its Study burrow inside the real Planner surface, and Open in App preserves the burrow selection and canonical item identities.

concreteNamedSourceContexts.text: The focused-card view retains partially visible, shadowed neighbours. Vertical scrolling is the default; horizontal navigation is a persisted option. Provide keyboard/touch navigation, the floating search bar and the subject/topic sidebar without obstructing content. Edit mode uses click-to-edit and an explicit Flip button. View mode uses click-to-flip and cannot mutate card content; rating is permitted as personal review state. The AI bar's Write setting does not override the host's View restriction.

Required operations are create/open/save, edit either side, add/duplicate/reorder/remove/restore cards, bulk create/edit, search/filter, set/topic/custom grouping, asset insertion, drawing, rate/review, import/export and settings. Bulk edits expose exact per-item results where partial success is allowed; destructive bulk changes have impact preview and the inherited approval rules. Undo/redo and interrupted-save recovery preserve the prior valid revision.

A rating MUST persist on the card's personal review record. When a valid Study topic link exists, it MUST submit attributed evidence to the existing Study service and update linked views. An unlinked card remains usable and offers topic linking rather than fabricating a mapping. Shared deck edits do not overwrite other users' review records. Inline Spaces flashcards and Revision Bank entries must be able to open/save the same canonical set.
